top_news.title: UN: Burundi Set to Win Human Rights Council Seat Despite Abuses
top_news.summary: Click to expand Image Burundi's President Evariste Ndayishimiye speaks during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, in New York, New York, September 23, 2026. 2026 AP Photo/Heather Khalifa (New York) - Burundi is set to win re-election to the United Nations Human Rights Council in a vote on October 12, 2026, with no competition, Human Rights Watch said today. Burundi is seeking to retain its seat even though the government of this Central African country has not improved its abusive human rights conditions. Burundi is one of the four African countries running for the same number of seats on the 47-nation council. The regional slates for the Western group, Latin America and the Caribbean, Central and Eastern Europe, and Asia also lack competition. This effectively guarantees all 15 candidates, fit or unfit, spots on the UN's premier rights body for three years beginning on January 1, 2027. "This uncompetitive vote makes a mockery of the word 'election,'" said Louis Charbonneau, UN director at Human Rights Watch. "UN member states should insist on competitive slates so they can reject candidates with poor human rights records. No one should have a seat on this crucial body handed to them on a silver platter." Ghana, Nigeria, and Zambia are candidates for Africa's other three available seats. In Asia, Japan, Jordan, Kuwait, and Nepal are running for the region's four seats. In Latin America and the Caribbean, Brazil, the Dominican Republic, and Uruguay are set to take the region's three spots. For the Western group, Germany and Ireland are on track to get the group's two available seats, while Moldova and Ukraine will take Central and Eastern Europe's two spots. Despite some positive government statements, Burundi has not carried out meaningful reform to address longstanding concerns related to governance, justice, or accountability. Grave abuses persist with impunity, including extrajudicial executions, enforced disappearances, arbitrary arrests, and detention. Freedom of expression, assembly, and association remain severely restricted. Burundi is in the third year of its current term and is allowed to run for another consecutive term. On October 6, the country's delegation tried to use their membership to prevent UN scrutiny of Burundi's poor human rights record, first by calling a vote to renew the mandate of the UN special rapporteur on Burundi and then by voting against it. The resolution was adopted, though, 22 to 7, with 17 abstentions. That resolution not only expressed concerns about ongoing rights violations but highlighted Burundi's refusal to cooperate with the council and most of its mechanisms, including the special rapporteur. General AssemblyResolution 60/251, which created the Human Rights Council in 2006, says that countries voting for members should "take into account the contribution of candidates to the promotion and protection of human rights." Council members are required to "uphold the highest standards in the promotion and protection of human rights" at home and abroad and to "fully cooperate with the Council." Candidates only need a simple majority in the secret-ballot vote in the 193-nation General Assembly to secure a seat on the Human Rights Council. That makes it highly unlikely that any candidate will lose, no matter how unqualified. Nevertheless, UN member states should not cast votes for abusive governments that are demonstrably unqualified for council membership. Among the other candidates, Nigeria should ensure accountability for serious international crimes committed by all parties-including security forces-during the conflict with the armed group Boko Haram. Brazil should investigate and curb police abuse after law enforcement officers set a grim record in 2025 by killing more than 6,500 people, the vast majority of them Black. Ukraine has suffered countless atrocities committed by Russian forces on its territory since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. At the same time, Ukrainian authorities have unjustly prosecuted Ukrainian civilians living under Russian occupation, including teachers, medics, municipal workers, and volunteers for doing essential work that international humanitarian law permits civilians to perform under occupation. The Human Rights Council scrutinizes all UN member states' rights records in the Universal Periodic Review process. In November 2025, the United States refused to participate in its review. If the US government does not participate in its rescheduled review in November, it will become the first member country not to complete its review. The Human Rights Council has played a crucial role in ensuring independent investigations of abuses inSyria,Myanmar,North Korea, Russia, Ukraine, Israel/Palestine, Afghanistan, Sudan, and elsewhere. Council members should press for investigations of abuses by other countries in need of scrutiny, including major powers. These should includeChina's crimes against humanity against Uyghurs and others inXinjiang, as well as the US military's unlawful strikes targeting vessels the Caribbean and Pacific, amounting to extrajudicial killings. The council should also explore possible action to support global justice in the face of a US assault on international accountability mechanisms. The US on October 9 imposed unjustified sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC). The Trump administration has made clear its aim to destroy the ICC to shield US and Israeli officials from facing charges before the court. The US had previously sanctioned ICC officials, Francesca Albanese, the UN special rapporteur on human rights in the Palestinian Territory occupied since 1967, and several prominent Palestinian human rights groups. "The human rights movement is under increasing attack by powerful governments, including established democracies," Charbonneau said. "The Human Rights Council has done victims of human rights abuses a huge service with investigations that often deter governments and armed groups from committing violations. We need the council now more than ever."

The preparation team, headed by Dr. Ekniti Nitithanprapas, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance, alongside Dr. Vinit Visessuvanapoom, Director General of the Fiscal Policy Office, and Mr. Nadhavudh Dhamasiri, Deputy Director General of the Fiscal Policy Office, guided members of the press through the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center (QSNCC) to showcase the venue's full readiness for the meetings. With preparations completed on all fronts ahead of the official handover to the IMF and the World Bank, Thailand is set to open its doors to over 15,000 policymakers, economists, government officials, private sector executives, and media representatives from 191 countries who are coming together to jointly shape the direction of the global economy. Dr. Ekniti Nitithanprapas, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance, stated that Thailand will open its doors next week from 12 - 18 October 2026 to welcome world economic and financial leaders as host of the 2026 IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings. Hosting this gathering is akin to bringing the global headquarters of the IMF and the World Bank Group from Washington, D.C., directly to Thailand. For this milestone occasion, the Thai government has not only prepared facilities and infrastructure to the highest international standards, but has also integrated advanced technology and digital innovation, while infusing Thailand's distinctive identity and culture-including warmth, friendship, and the meticulous care of Thai Hospitality-into every aspect of the welcome, creating a lasting impression and underscoring Thailand's standing on the world stage. Regarding venue readiness, the QSNCC has elevated its operations to international benchmarks. Highlights include a state-of-the-art Master Control Room and broadcast transmission systems built to the same caliber as major global events like the FIFA World Cup and UEFA Champions League, managed by an elite team with direct operational experience from the World Economic Forum in Davos. Concurrently, the highest level of security is being implemented in close coordination with the Royal Thai Police through a multi-tiered security zoning system, featuring 17 X-ray checkpoints, 19 walk-through security gates, and integrated 24-hour CCTV surveillance. Dedicated security personnel are also stationed around the clock across all 21 official delegate hotels. To date, registration has exceeded 15,000 attendees and continues to increase, reflecting the international community's confidence in convening in Thailand to set the agenda for the global economy. Dr. Ekniti added that beyond generating an immediate economic injection of approximately THB 1.05 billion to 2.25 billion-driven by an estimated 15,000 attendees staying an average of 7-10 days with a daily expenditure of THB 10,000-15,000 per person distributed across tourism, hotels, restaurants, and local community products-the Annual Meetings also open the door to the nation's economic future by showcasing Thailand's potential as a regional investment hub for future industries in Southeast Asia. The government will seize this opportunity to highlight its readiness in digital infrastructure, clean energy, and investment incentives to attract Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) into target industries, such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Electric Vehicles (EV), which will serve as new growth engines driving the economy and sustainably elevating national competitiveness. In addition, the event highlights Thai Soft Power and culture through venue decor adorned with 40 traditional Thai textile patterns from 28 communities across 21 provinces-such as Tai Lue woven fabric, elephant-patterned Pha Khao Ma, and batik featuring the "Buppha Borom Rachineenart" pattern (Queen Mother Floral Batik) as well as Cattleya Queen Sirikit (a hybrid orchid named in honor of Her Majesty Queen Sirikit The Queen Mother)-reflecting the value of Thai local wisdom on the world stage. Also on display are two "Impact Piece" sculptures, each of which weaves natural materials with indigenous craftsmanship to symbolize unity, cooperation, and sustainable progress. Furthermore, the culinary program features certified Thai Geographical Indication (GI) products, allowing international delegates to experience distinctive local flavors through specially crafted items, including "AM Brew" coffee made with premium Thai beans and "Thai Tea by QSNCC," meticulously prepared with high-quality domestic ingredients. Dr. Vinit Visessuvanapoom, Director-General of the Fiscal Policy Office, addressed the "Green Meeting" initiative, noting that Thailand and QSNCC-a certified green building facility-are committed to delivering an environmentally friendly conference through concrete actions. These include providing a dedicated fleet of over 320 electric vehicles (EVs) for attendees, projected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by more than 95.8 metric tons of CO equivalent (tCOeq), comparable to planting over 9,580 mature trees; circular waste management that upcycles food waste into organic fertilizer; a paperless digital meeting system; and significantly reducing single-use plastics across all catering operations. articles.title: UN: Burundi Set to Win Human Rights Council Seat Despite Abuses
articles.summary: Click to expand Image Burundi's President Evariste Ndayishimiye speaks during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, in New York, New York, September 23, 2026. 2026 AP Photo/Heather Khalifa (New York) - Burundi is set to win re-election to the United Nations Human Rights Council in a vote on October 12, 2026, with no competition, Human Rights Watch said today. Burundi is seeking to retain its seat even though the government of this Central African country has not improved its abusive human rights conditions. Burundi is one of the four African countries running for the same number of seats on the 47-nation council. "UN member states should insist on competitive slates so they can reject candidates with poor human rights records. No one should have a seat on this crucial body handed to them on a silver platter." Ghana, Nigeria, and Zambia are candidates for Africa's other three available seats. In Asia, Japan, Jordan, Kuwait, and Nepal are running for the region's four seats. In Latin America and the Caribbean, Brazil, the Dominican Republic, and Uruguay are set to take the region's three spots. Despite some positive government statements, Burundi has not carried out meaningful reform to address longstanding concerns related to governance, justice, or accountability. General AssemblyResolution 60/251, which created the Human Rights Council in 2006, says that countries voting for members should "take into account the contribution of candidates to the promotion and protection of human rights." Council members are required to "uphold the highest standards in the promotion and protection of human rights" at home and abroad and to "fully cooperate with the Council." Candidates only need a simple majority in the secret-ballot vote in the 193-nation General Assembly to secure a seat on the Human Rights Council. That makes it highly unlikely that any candidate will lose, no matter how unqualified. Nevertheless, UN member states should not cast votes for abusive governments that are demonstrably unqualified for council membership. Among the other candidates, Nigeria should ensure accountability for serious international crimes committed by all parties-including security forces-during the conflict with the armed group Boko Haram. Brazil should investigate and curb police abuse after law enforcement officers set a grim record in 2025 by killing more than 6,500 people, the vast majority of them Black. Ukraine has suffered countless atrocities committed by Russian forces on its territory since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. If the US government does not participate in its rescheduled review in November, it will become the first member country not to complete its review. The Human Rights Council has played a crucial role in ensuring independent investigations of abuses inSyria,Myanmar,North Korea, Russia, Ukraine, Israel/Palestine, Afghanistan, Sudan, and elsewhere. Council members should press for investigations of abuses by other countries in need of scrutiny, including major powers. These should includeChina's crimes against humanity against Uyghurs and others inXinjiang, as well as the US military's unlawful strikes targeting vessels the Caribbean and Pacific, amounting to extrajudicial killings. The council should also explore possible action to support global justice in the face of a US assault on international accountability mechanisms. The Trump administration has made clear its aim to destroy the ICC to shield US and Israeli officials from facing charges before the court. articles.title: Finance Minister Guides Press Through QSNCC Ahead of 2026 IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings, Reaffirming Thailand
articles.summary: The Ministry of Finance of Thailand and the Bank of Thailand are involved in preparations for the 2026 Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group-an event, given its scale, often dubbed the "Olympics of Finance." The preparation team, headed by Dr. Ekniti Nitithanprapas, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance, alongside Dr. Vinit Visessuvanapoom, Director General of the Fiscal Policy Office, and Mr. Nadhavudh Dhamasiri, Deputy Director General of the Fiscal Policy Office, guided members of the press through the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center (QSNCC) to showcase the venue's full readiness for the meetings. With preparations completed on all fronts ahead of the official handover to the IMF and the World Bank, Thailand is set to open its doors to over 15,000 policymakers, economists, government officials, private sector executives, and media representatives from 191 countries who are coming together to jointly shape the direction of the global economy. Dr. Ekniti Nitithanprapas, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance, stated that Thailand will open its doors next week from 12 - 18 October 2026 to welcome world economic and financial leaders as host of the 2026 IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings. Hosting this gathering is akin to bringing the global headquarters of the IMF and the World Bank Group from Washington, D.C., directly to Thailand. For this milestone occasion, the Thai government has not only prepared facilities and infrastructure to the highest international standards, but has also integrated advanced technology and digital innovation, while infusing Thailand's distinctive identity and culture-including warmth, friendship, and the meticulous care of Thai Hospitality-into every aspect of the welcome, creating a lasting impression and underscoring Thailand's standing on the world stage. Regarding venue readiness, the QSNCC has elevated its operations to international benchmarks. Highlights include a state-of-the-art Master Control Room and broadcast transmission systems built to the same caliber as major global events like the FIFA World Cup and UEFA Champions League, managed by an elite team with direct operational experience from the World Economic Forum in Davos. Dedicated security personnel are also stationed around the clock across all 21 official delegate hotels. To date, registration has exceeded 15,000 attendees and continues to increase, reflecting the international community's confidence in convening in Thailand to set the agenda for the global economy. Dr. Ekniti added that beyond generating an immediate economic injection of approximately THB 1.05 billion to 2.25 billion-driven by an estimated 15,000 attendees staying an average of 7-10 days with a daily expenditure of THB 10,000-15,000 per person distributed across tourism, hotels, restaurants, and local community products-the Annual Meetings also open the door to the nation's economic future by showcasing Thailand's potential as a regional investment hub for future industries in Southeast Asia. Also on display are two "Impact Piece" sculptures, each of which weaves natural materials with indigenous craftsmanship to symbolize unity, cooperation, and sustainable progress. Furthermore, the culinary program features certified Thai Geographical Indication (GI) products, allowing international delegates to experience distinctive local flavors through specially crafted items, including "AM Brew" coffee made with premium Thai beans and "Thai Tea by QSNCC," meticulously prepared with high-quality domestic ingredients.
